mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates easy monetary policy, which may stimulate investment and consumption, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher when FEDFUNDS is low (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment rate signals economic recovery, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative when UNRATE drops as specified.

mechanism_narrative: Combined improvement in unemployment and payroll employment indicates a strong labor market, positively affecting S&P 500.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between labor improvements and SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary easing cycle, low FEDFUNDS stimulates equity markets, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not higher during easing periods.

mechanism_narrative: Growth in payroll employment signals economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: No positive correlation between PAYEMS growth and SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth indicates high demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are negative when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2%.

mechanism_narrative: Rising inflation with low interest rates may indicate stagflation, negatively affecting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: SPX returns are positive under specified conditions.

mechanism_narrative: High industrial production indicates strong supply, boosting S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX returns are not higher when INDPRO is high.
